passage:
Mentor's note, Saturday. Amandeep writing about Seema and the tax notice.
The notice claimed more income than Seema thought had been earned. Seema arrived with a folder and a nervous laugh. On the table went Form 16, twelve monthly pay slips, and printed bank statements.
I did not advise. I asked Seema to compare the notice to the papers, line by line, with a ruler under each line. Forty minutes in, Seema stopped. "This bonus is listed twice. Once in the salary, once again under other income."
Seema drew a circle round it and drafted a reply to send through the official portal, attaching the papers. I suggested a qualified practitioner read the reply before it went.
— Amandeep

qa.a: Seema was nervous, shown by the nervous laugh, and then focused once the line-by-line check began.

qa.q: What could Seema do if the tax office still disagrees after the reply?
qa.a: Seema could ask the qualified practitioner how to respond further and keep all the papers together.

qa.q: What is it like for Amandeep to sit with Seema during the check?
qa.a: Amandeep holds back from giving advice, watching Seema find the double entry alone, which lets Seema own the discovery.

Tuesday night
Spread everything on the bed tonight: twelve salary slips, the Form 16 from the office, two bank statements, and the notice that's been scaring me since Friday. Jahnavi di sat with me with a highlighter, which made it bearable.
The notice says my income was 2,40,000 more than I declared. Impossible. So, one line at a time: the salary slips add up to exactly what's in the Form 16. Bank statements: salary credits match every month. Then Jahnavi di spotted it. The notice lists my salary under the old company AND the same amount again under a new employer code. The company was bought and renamed in October; I never changed jobs. Same money, counted twice.
I can breathe again. Tomorrow I'll write it up with the two slips side by side and ask the CA uncle to check my reply.
Irawati

qa.q: How much more income did the notice say Irawati had?
How did Irawati feel before and after the mismatch was found?
qa.a: Irawati had been scared since Friday, then felt relieved and able to breathe once the double entry was found.

qa.q: What else could make Irawati's reply stronger?
qa.a: Attaching the two slips side by side and a letter from the company about the renaming, and having the CA check it, would make the error easy to see.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi feel after the evening?
qa.a: Jahnavi made the evening bearable and spotted the double entry, so she might feel proud and relieved for her younger sibling.

grounding: It shows a person collecting salary slips, Form 16 and bank statements, comparing them with a notice and finding one income counted twice.

Madhuri: ok I've got all of it out. salary slips, form 16, 3 bank statements, and the famous notice 😩
Deepika: good. what does the notice say you missed?
Madhuri: 38,000 of interest income
Madhuri: but I DID declare my FD interest. 19,000
Deepika: open the bank's interest certificate. how much?
Madhuri: 19,000. exactly.
Deepika: now look at the notice again. one line or two?
Madhuri: wait. two lines. 19,000 from the Andheri branch. 19,000 from... the same account number??
Deepika: same account, two entries
Madhuri: so it got counted twice?? when I moved the FD to the new branch?
Deepika: sounds like it. screenshot both lines and the certificate, and have your CA check the reply before you send it
Madhuri: I've been crying about this since Sunday and it's a duplicate 😅

qa.q: How much interest income did the notice say Madhuri missed?
How did Madhuri feel on finding the duplicate?
qa.a: Madhuri felt a rush of relief mixed with embarrassment 😅 after days of worry over what turned out to be a double entry.

qa.q: What else could Madhuri do so the next branch move doesn't cause this?
qa.a: Madhuri could note account changes with dates and check the yearly tax statement early, so a duplicate is caught before any notice.

qa.q: How might Deepika see the way this chat went?
qa.a: Deepika guided with simple questions rather than answers, and probably feels glad to see a friend calm down.

grounding: It shows a person gathering slips, Form 16 and statements and comparing them with a notice until one income entry turns out to be counted twice.
